correctness.rationale: The transfer identity is obtained by counting all odd lifts in each permitted residue class and subtracting precisely the two prime-r forbidden lifts; the CRT parity argument proves invariance modulo 2pq for every prime r>pq. The two complete finite residue certificates are checked by independently constructing each forbidden lift and by direct gcd enumeration. Dirichlet implies infinitely many primes in both coprime progressions. Boundary r>pq is explicit and neither finite experiment nor a search is used in place of infinitude proof.

originality.rationale: Renshaw Theorem 3 gives the support-dependent universal error bound; neither its statement nor subsequent inspected discussion establishes two-sided equality on infinitely many squarefree supports with exactly three distinct primes. The new residue-parity transfer and two explicit coprime prime progressions provide the missing sharpness witnesses. All nine actual published-finding corpus searches, targeted literature searches and deduplicated accessible historical claims gave no implication-dominating theorem; unindexed equivalent results remain a residual historical risk.

value.rationale: Showing a universal error bound is genuinely optimal on both sides, not just at isolated examples but along two infinite prime families, resolves a natural quantitative sharpness question left by the recent theorem. It explains optimality structurally through a parity-residue transfer, rather than an arbitrary finite cutoff, and does not overclaim extremizer classification.
